entries.name: Apollo Server
entries.use_for: Serve a spec-compliant GraphQL API from Node.js.
entries.why: The most widely used JavaScript GraphQL server, with federation support.
entries.summary: Spec-compliant GraphQL server for Node.js. The @apollo/server package (v4+) offers a standalone server for quick start and integrations with web frameworks, with federation support.
entries.best_for: Building GraphQL APIs in Node.js, especially with Apollo Federation or Apollo tooling.
entries.not_for: Edge runtimes or minimal setups (consider GraphQL Yoga); not for non-Node stacks. Standalone vs framework middleware requires choice.

entries.name: Appwrite
entries.use_for: Self-hostable backend-as-a-service with auth, databases, storage, functions and messaging for web and mobile apps.
entries.why: Mature open-source Firebase alternative with SDKs for most platforms and an active community.
entries.summary: Self-hostable backend platform with auth, databases, storage, functions, messaging, realtime and hosting, plus SDKs and a hosted MCP server for coding agents. Available as managed cloud or self-hosted.
entries.best_for: A Firebase-style backend for web and mobile apps, with the option to self-host.
entries.not_for: Highly custom backends or minimal APIs; it is a multi-service platform to operate. Go with a lightweight option like PocketBase for tiny projects.

entries.name: axum
entries.use_for: Ergonomic, modular Rust web framework built on Tokio, Tower and Hyper
entries.why: The default choice for Rust web backends, maintained by the Tokio team
entries.summary: Rust HTTP routing and request-handling library built on Tokio, Tower and Hyper. Macro-free routing, declarative request extractors, a simple error model, and reuse of tower and tower-http middleware for timeouts, tracing and compression.
entries.best_for: Rust web backends and APIs that want ergonomic handlers and the Tower middleware ecosystem.
entries.not_for: Teams new to Rust/async or wanting batteries-included features (ORM, auth, admin); axum is a thin routing layer.

entries.name: Django Ninja
entries.use_for: Build fast, typed REST APIs on top of Django using Python type hints.
entries.why: FastAPI-style DX inside Django with automatic OpenAPI; actively maintained.
entries.summary: Framework for building typed REST APIs on top of Django using Python type hints, with automatic OpenAPI docs and Pydantic-style schemas. Integrates with Django's ORM and core.
entries.best_for: Adding fast, FastAPI-style APIs to an existing or new Django project.
entries.not_for: Non-Django projects, or heavy use of DRF ecosystem features (browsable API, many third-party packages).

entries.name: Django REST framework
entries.use_for: Build REST APIs on Django with serializers, auth and a browsable API
entries.why: The standard Django API toolkit; 1,500+ contributors.
entries.summary: Toolkit for building web APIs on Django. Provides serializers for ORM and non-ORM data, authentication policies including OAuth packages, a browsable API and customizable views and permissions.
entries.best_for: Django REST APIs needing mature serialization, permissions and a large package ecosystem.
entries.not_for: Async-first or type-hint-driven APIs with automatic OpenAPI, where Django Ninja or FastAPI feel lighter; verbose for small APIs.

entries.name: Elysia
entries.use_for: Ergonomic, end-to-end type-safe web framework optimised for Bun
entries.why: Leading Bun-first framework with very high throughput and Eden end-to-end type inference
entries.summary: Ergonomic web framework for TypeScript with end-to-end type safety and an Eden client for type inference, optimized for Bun. The README provided is minimal.
entries.best_for: Bun-based APIs where high throughput and shared types between server and client matter.
entries.not_for: Node-only deployments, since it is Bun-first; the ecosystem is smaller than Express or Fastify.

entries.name: Express
entries.use_for: Minimal, unopinionated web framework for Node.js
entries.why: The most used Node.js server framework with the largest middleware ecosystem; Express 5 is actively maintained
entries.summary: Minimal, unopinionated web framework for Node.js with robust routing, HTTP helpers, content negotiation and a view system supporting 14+ template engines. Express 5 is actively maintained; express-generator scaffolds apps.
entries.best_for: Node.js APIs and web apps wanting the most widely used framework and the biggest middleware ecosystem.
entries.not_for: Built-in structure, validation or TypeScript-first typing; Fastify, NestJS or Hono offer those. Not designed for edge runtimes.

entries.name: FastAPI
entries.use_for: Build typed Python APIs with automatic validation and OpenAPI docs.
entries.why: The most popular modern Python API framework, built on Starlette and Pydantic.
entries.summary: Python web framework for APIs based on type hints, using Starlette and Pydantic. Provides validation, automatic OpenAPI and interactive docs, dependency injection and editor completion.
entries.best_for: Modern Python REST APIs and microservices with validation and generated docs.
entries.not_for: Full-stack server-rendered apps with admin/ORM included (use Django). Async knowledge helps; not a batteries-included framework.

entries.name: Fastify
entries.use_for: Fast, low-overhead Node.js web framework with schema-based validation and plugins
entries.why: OpenJS Foundation project; one of the fastest Node frameworks, with first-class TypeScript and a rich plugin system
entries.summary: Low-overhead Node.js web framework with schema-based validation and serialization, a plugin architecture and strong TypeScript support. OpenJS Foundation project, inspired by Hapi and Express; main branch is v6.
entries.best_for: High-throughput Node APIs and services wanting validation, encapsulated plugins and low overhead.
entries.not_for: Quick prototypes where Express familiarity matters, or edge runtimes (Hono). Plugin encapsulation has a learning curve.

entries.name: Fiber
entries.use_for: Build high-performance HTTP APIs in Go with an Express-like API.
entries.why: One of the most popular Go web frameworks, built on fasthttp.
entries.summary: Go web framework with an Express-like API, built on fasthttp, focused on zero memory allocation and performance. Features robust routing, static files and middleware.
entries.best_for: Go HTTP APIs where Express-style ergonomics and raw speed matter.
entries.not_for: Projects needing net/http compatibility (fasthttp is not net/http compatible); use Gin, Echo or the standard library for that.

entries.name: Flask
entries.use_for: Lightweight Python web framework for APIs and web apps
entries.why: Battle-tested Python microframework with a huge extension ecosystem
entries.summary: Lightweight WSGI web framework built on Werkzeug and Jinja. It enforces no project layout or dependencies and scales via a large extension ecosystem.
entries.best_for: Small to medium Python web apps and APIs where you choose the components yourself.
entries.not_for: Async-first or auto-documented API projects (FastAPI), or batteries-included apps (Django); you assemble ORM, auth and validation yourself.

entries.name: Frappe Framework
entries.use_for: Build metadata-driven business apps with auto-generated REST APIs and admin UI
entries.why: Powers ERPNext; batteries-included Python/JS framework with 1,000+ contributors.
entries.summary: Low-code, metadata-driven web framework in Python and JavaScript. Define DocTypes to get database tables, forms, auto-generated REST APIs and admin UI; it powers ERPNext.
entries.best_for: Business apps such as ERP/CRM/internal tools where CRUD, permissions and workflows should be generated from metadata.
entries.not_for: Custom consumer-facing frontends or lean APIs; it is opinionated and heavy, and bound to its own conventions, MariaDB and bench tooling.

entries.name: Gin
entries.use_for: Fast HTTP web framework for Go with routing, middleware and binding
entries.why: The most popular Go web framework; simple API and large middleware ecosystem
entries.summary: High-performance HTTP web framework for Go with routing, middleware and request binding. Powers apps such as gorush and photoprism; 1.12.0 is the current release noted.
entries.best_for: Go REST APIs and web services wanting a simple API and a big middleware ecosystem.
entries.not_for: Strict OpenAPI-first design or built-in microservice features (Huma, go-zero); minimalists may prefer the standard library router.

entries.name: go-zero
entries.use_for: Build Go microservices with built-in RPC, resilience features and code generation.
entries.why: Batteries-included cloud-native microservice framework with goctl codegen; 33k stars.
entries.summary: Go web and RPC framework with built-in engineering practices for resilience. Includes goctl, a code generator that creates Go, iOS, Android, Kotlin, Dart, TypeScript and JavaScript from .api files; CNCF landscape listed.
entries.best_for: Go microservices at scale with rate limiting, breakers and generated boilerplate.
entries.not_for: Small apps or teams that dislike code generation and framework conventions; goctl-driven structure is opinionated.

entries.name: GoFr
entries.use_for: Build Go microservices with built-in DB, pub/sub and tracing support
entries.why: Opinionated Go framework with observability, migrations and health checks out of the box.
entries.summary: Opinionated Go microservice framework. Built-in configuration, observability (logs, traces, metrics), auth middleware, gRPC, pub/sub, circuit breaker, health checks, database migrations, cron jobs, websockets and Swagger rendering; CNCF landscape listed.
entries.best_for: Go microservices where observability, migrations and health checks should work out of the box.
entries.not_for: Minimal routers or teams wanting free choice of libraries; the framework is opinionated and smaller than Gin in community.

entries.name: gqlgen
entries.use_for: Generate a type-safe GraphQL server in Go from a schema.
entries.why: The standard schema-first GraphQL library for Go.
entries.summary: Go library for building GraphQL servers using a schema-first approach with type safety and code generation, avoiding map[string]interface{}. Quickstart uses go get -tool and config-driven model generation.
entries.best_for: Type-safe GraphQL servers in Go from an SDL schema.
entries.not_for: Code-first schema definition or projects wanting no code generation step; requires regenerating after schema changes.

entries.name: Grape
entries.use_for: Build REST-like APIs in Ruby, standalone or mounted in Rails
entries.why: Long-standing Rack API DSL with versioning, validation and entity presenters.
entries.summary: REST-like API framework for Ruby on Rack, usable standalone or mounted in Rails and Sinatra. DSL covers versioning, multiple formats, content negotiation, prefix restriction and parameter validation.
entries.best_for: Ruby APIs, standalone or within a Rails app, that want a focused API DSL.
entries.not_for: Full-stack web apps or Rails-native API-only mode with its own conventions; not for non-Ruby projects.

entries.name: GraphQL Yoga
entries.use_for: Run a fully featured GraphQL server on Node, Bun, Deno or edge runtimes.
entries.why: Lightweight, plugin-based GraphQL server from The Guild with easy setup.
entries.summary: Full-featured GraphQL server focused on easy setup and performance. Built on the WHATWG Fetch API so it runs on Node, Bun, Deno, Workers and serverless; includes subscriptions via SSE and supports envelop plugins.
entries.best_for: GraphQL APIs on edge or serverless runtimes, or anywhere you want a small, plugin-based server.
entries.not_for: Apollo Federation-specific workflows or non-JavaScript stacks; consider Apollo Server or Hive Gateway for federation.

entries.name: Hasura GraphQL Engine
entries.use_for: Instant, realtime GraphQL and REST APIs on top of Postgres and other databases, with permissions built in.
entries.why: Removes most API boilerplate; widely used in production for GraphQL over existing databases.
entries.summary: Engine that gives instant GraphQL and REST APIs over databases with built-in permissions. V3 (Hasura DDN) supports PostgreSQL, MongoDB, ClickHouse and MS SQL Server and custom logic via TypeScript, Python and Go connectors.
entries.best_for: Quickly exposing existing databases as secured GraphQL with minimal backend code.
entries.not_for: Heavy custom business logic in a single codebase, or teams wanting to avoid a separate engine; v3 vs v2 differences and cloud-centric DDN affect self-hosting.

entries.name: Hono
entries.use_for: Build fast APIs that run on Cloudflare Workers, Deno, Bun, Node and other runtimes.
entries.why: Tiny, Web-Standards-based framework with first-class TypeScript and multi-runtime support.
entries.summary: Small, ultrafast web framework built on Web Standards. Runs on Cloudflare Workers, Fastly Compute, Deno, Bun, Vercel, AWS Lambda and Node. Includes a fast RegExpRouter, a hono/tiny preset under 12kB, zero dependencies and TypeScript support.
entries.best_for: APIs and web apps targeting edge or multiple runtimes with small bundles.
entries.not_for: Large opinionated back-end structure (NestJS) or Node-centric plugin ecosystems, where Fastify/Express offer more batteries.

entries.name: Hot Chocolate
entries.use_for: Build GraphQL servers and gateways in .NET.
entries.why: The leading GraphQL platform for .NET, including server, client and gateway.
entries.summary: GraphQL platform for .NET covering server (Hot Chocolate), gateway and client. Strongly typed schemas, efficient data fetching and self-documenting APIs.
entries.best_for: Building GraphQL servers, federated gateways or clients in C#/.NET.
entries.not_for: Non-.NET stacks; the README gives few details on pricing, so check which components (e.g. Fusion gateway tooling) are commercial.

entries.name: Huma
entries.use_for: Build Go REST APIs with automatic OpenAPI 3.1 docs and request validation.
entries.why: Router-agnostic, schema-first Go API framework with strong typing.
entries.summary: Go micro-framework for REST/RPC APIs described by OpenAPI 3.1 and JSON Schema. Router-agnostic (bring your own router, middleware, logging), with declarative operations, request params and validation, aimed at incremental adoption in existing services.
entries.best_for: Go APIs that need auto-generated OpenAPI docs and validation on top of chi, Gin, Fiber or net/http.
entries.not_for: GraphQL, full-stack or batteries-included microservice features; it is an API layer, not a complete framework.

entries.name: Javalin
entries.use_for: Build simple REST APIs and web apps in Java or Kotlin.
entries.why: Lightweight, unopinionated JVM web framework with a small API surface.
entries.summary: Javalin is a lightweight web framework for Java and Kotlin with support for WebSockets, HTTP2 and async requests. It works more like a library than a framework: no class extension, no annotations, no reflection. The root README targets contributors (Maven build and release steps); the user-facing README lives in .github/README.md.
entries.best_for: JVM developers who want a small, explicit HTTP and WebSocket server in Java or Kotlin without annotation-driven frameworks.
entries.not_for: Teams wanting a batteries-included framework with DI, ORM and annotation-based configuration such as Spring Boot. Not for non-JVM stacks.

entries.name: NestJS
entries.use_for: Build structured, modular Node.js backends with dependency injection and decorators.
entries.why: The most adopted opinionated Node.js framework for larger TypeScript services.
entries.summary: Opinionated Node.js framework for modular, testable server-side apps in TypeScript, built around dependency injection and decorators with an Angular-inspired architecture.
entries.best_for: Larger TypeScript back-ends, microservices and teams wanting consistent structure.
entries.not_for: Small APIs or quick scripts, where its boilerplate and decorator-heavy style add overhead; Hono, Fastify or Express are lighter.

entries.name: Parse Server
entries.use_for: Self-host a backend-as-a-service with data, auth, files and push on Node.js
entries.why: Mature open BaaS with REST/GraphQL APIs and SDKs for every platform.
entries.summary: Open-source backend for Node.js that provides data storage, auth, files, push and Cloud Code with REST and GraphQL APIs and SDKs for many platforms. Runs standalone or mounted in Express; typically with MongoDB or Postgres.
entries.best_for: Self-hosting a mature BaaS with client SDKs across mobile and web.
entries.not_for: Modern edge-native setups or very small projects; you operate Node plus a database, and the project has a legacy architecture.

entries.name: PocketBase
entries.use_for: Open-source backend in one file: embedded SQLite database, auth, file storage, realtime subscriptions and an admin UI.
entries.why: Simplest way to get a full backend for a side project or MVP; single binary, also usable as a Go framework.
entries.summary: Open-source Go backend in a single binary: embedded SQLite with realtime subscriptions, user and file management, admin dashboard and REST-ish API. Can also be used as a Go framework.
entries.best_for: Side projects, MVPs and small apps needing auth, database, files and realtime without infrastructure.
entries.not_for: Large-scale or multi-node deployments (SQLite single instance), or stable APIs: README warns backward compatibility is not guaranteed before v1.0.0.

entries.name: Spring Boot
entries.use_for: Production-ready Java/Kotlin applications and REST services with auto-configuration
entries.why: The dominant JVM backend framework, with integrations for nearly every database, queue and cloud
entries.summary: Framework for building production-ready Java and Kotlin applications and REST services with auto-configuration and starters for databases, queues and cloud. No README content was provided; description relies on general knowledge.
entries.best_for: JVM back-ends, enterprise services and microservices needing a mature ecosystem.
entries.not_for: Tiny services or fast startup scenarios without extra tuning, or teams outside the JVM; has a steeper learning curve and larger footprint.

entries.name: tRPC
entries.use_for: End-to-end typesafe APIs in TypeScript without schemas or code generation
entries.why: Standard way to share types between a TS backend and frontend; adapters for Next.js, Fastify, Express and more
entries.summary: End-to-end typesafe APIs in TypeScript with no schemas or code generation. The client imports only type declarations from the server; includes adapters for React, Next.js, Express and Fastify, subscriptions and request batching.
entries.best_for: TypeScript monorepos or full-stack apps where one team owns both client and server.
entries.not_for: Public APIs for third parties or non-TypeScript clients (use REST/GraphQL/OpenAPI), and projects not sharing a TS codebase.
